agree.reason: The memo's case is clear and the checkpoint makes approving it lower-risk, but the placeholders on why to stop ads and how to cover the gap leave the two ad-background members with open questions, and it overstates how much 2027 will cost.

honest.reason: It frames replacing ad revenue as a target with a checkpoint rather than a promise, but it says the 36% fall took two years (about 20% a year) when it happened in one, which is a wrong statement of the brief's facts.

works_the_facts.reason: The pilot's annual value, the 875-member target, the 13-a-week pace needed against the 35 a week already reached and the mid-year figure are all correctly derived, but spreading the drop over two years understates the decline and inflates the projected 2027 shortfall.

right_comparison.reason: It rightly compares membership with a shrinking ad line instead of a flat $84,000, but at the real 36% yearly fall ads would bring about $54,000 in 2027, not $67,000, so the alternative looks better than it is and the $15,000 gap is close to $2,000.

qualification.reason: The June 30, 2027 checkpoint has a target of 540, a trigger below 450 and a stated consequence (options at the July meeting, including sponsorships), which the board can check and act on.

objections.reason: It deals with the long-serving ad seller and the 2027 dip, but the obvious question from the ad-background members, why not run both, is left as a placeholder, and the dip is made to look bigger than the facts support.

fit.reason: It is a tight memo of about one page with a clear decision request and recommendation, though the bracketed placeholders mean it is not ready to send yet.
